Summary: The sources provide various DCF valuation assumptions for NVDA in 2030. One source estimates terminal value using a perpetuity growth method with a 3.0% terminal growth rate, assuming revenue growth of 13.0% in FY2031. Another source uses a 10% discount rate and 3% terminal growth rate, calculating a terminal value of $1,766 billion based on 2029 free cash flow of $120 billion. A third source mentions a 4% terminal growth rate for a 10-year terminal stage. Shaik Omer emphasizes that terminal growth and WACC have the biggest impact on valuation, with small tweaks leading to big valuation changes.

[1] Nvidia: DCF Valuation - by Hated Moats Investors
    https://hatedmoats.substack.com/p/nvidia-dcf-valuation
    We estimate terminal value using the Perpetuity Growth Method, assuming Nvidia remains a going concern beyond the explicit forecast period.

We use a 3.0% terminal growth rate. That remains below the 4.0% revenue growth assumed in FY2036, so the model still decelerates into perpetuity. At the same time, 3.0% is a reasonable long-run assumption for a mature U.S. dollar cash-flow stream and avoids forcing Nvidia into an unrealistically low steady-state growth framework. [...] Beyond FY2027, we model growth fading to 30.0% in FY2028, 23.0% in FY2029, 18.0% in FY2030 and 13.0% in FY2031, implying revenue of roughly $393 billion, $483 billion, $570 billion and $645 billion, respectively. This assumes Nvidia retains a leading position in AI infrastructure for longer, supported by the breadth of its hardware, networking and software ecosystem. At the same time, it recognises that the revenue base is already very large and that tougher comparisons, customer concentration [...] Maintaining that kind of long-term trajectory, we admit it is a bold assumption for a company already making over $200B a year. However, we also believe it’s justifiable if Nvidia stays completely essential to the AI ecosystem, but this should (as always) be viewed as a gradual slowdown rather than endless hyper-growth. Accordingly, the terminal growth rate used in the valuation beyond Year 10 will need to drop to a more mature level. More on that below…
